referents.why: First singular 'me' (lifnai, 'before me') in the psalm's own voice; the verse quotes no one, and 23:4 'with me' is the same voice.
First singular 'my' on the enemies (tsorerai); the psalm's own voice.
First singular 'my' on the head; the psalm's own voice.
First singular 'my' on the cup; the psalm's own voice.

Implied second masculine singular subject of the yiqtol 'you arrange'. The psalm speaks to God from 23:4 ('you are with me') and the LORD is the shepherd of 23:1. David also agrees in morphology, but he is not the one the psalm addresses.
Implied second masculine singular subject of the qatal 'you have refreshed', the same addressee as the clause before. The only sensible addressee is the LORD, as for cl0s.

groups.why: Two consecutive clauses, each with its subject carried only in the verb (you arrange; you have refreshed), are acts of one addressed agent. The subject is the LORD, so the group is flagged.

none_fit.what: Two images set side by side with no connective: the anointing of the head, then 'my cup overflows' as a nominal clause with its own subject. No link type marks bare juxtaposition, and 'parallel' needs the same subject in both lines.
